chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever kisses his child, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, writes for him a good deed; and whoever makes him happy, Allah will make him happy on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever teaches him the Quran, he will be called by the title of the two parents, so they will be clothed with two garments, from whose light the faces of the people of Paradise will shine.'

key_terms.دُعِيَ بِالْأَبَوَيْنِ: called by the title of the two parents

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for kissing, pleasing, and teaching the Quran to one's child in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the Prophetic tradition of nurturing children through physical affection and Quranic instruction, linking these acts to specific eschatological rewards. It highlights the unique status of Quran teachers, who are metaphorically called 'parents' and adorned with radiant garments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual lineage established through religious education.
